text: Do you know how three astronauts fell out of space at almost forty thousand kilometres an hour, and lived?
This is the real Apollo eleven capsule, Columbia. Laser scanned, inch by inch, by the Smithsonian.
It's only three point nine metres wide. Inside, three seats, for three men coming home from the Moon.
On the way back, it hit the air at about eleven kilometres every second.
The air in front can't get out of the way. It's squeezed so hard, it turns into glowing plasma.
That's why the bottom is blunt. It pushes a shock wave out in front, so most of the heat stays in the air.
The rest hits the heat shield. A honeycomb, filled with a resin called Avcoat.
It's built to burn. The surface chars, and melts away, and carries the heat with it.
Columbia left shiny silver. It came home scorched brown.
For about three minutes, the plasma blocked every radio signal. On the ground, they could only wait.
Inside, the crew were pressed into their seats, at six and a half g.
Then, two small drogue chutes. Then three main parachutes, each twenty-five metres across.
July twenty-fourth, nineteen sixty-nine. Columbia hit the Pacific at about thirty-five kilometres an hour.
It landed upside down. Three balloons turned it upright.
Losing the signal for a while is normal. What matters is picking up where you left off.
Orbi Transfer does that with your files. If the connection drops, the upload resumes, and only the missing parts are sent.
